entry.title: DTCC's tokenization service launches with 25 securities, backed by roughly $30 trillion in underlying assets
entry.summary:
According to materials published by DTCC, its tokenization service has opened with 25 tokenizable securities whose underlying DTC-custodied assets total roughly $30 trillion. The tokens correspond 1:1 to the original securities, carry the same CUSIP, and can be transferred peer-to-peer 24/7 between registered DTC wallets subject to compliance transfer restrictions, while DTC remains the official book of record.
Because the tokens keep the same CUSIP and the same rights and investor protections as book-entry securities, a slice of DTC-custodied assets — including Treasury coupon and maturity servicing — now runs on blockchain rails without DTC ceding its role as the official record keeper.
The first supported assets are Russell 1000 constituents (starting with some large-cap stocks), selected ETFs and U.S. Treasuries; Treasury interest and maturity servicing will occur on-chain, with payments made in fiat to participants' traditional accounts. Initial networks are Canton Network (CIP-56) and DTCC's private Besu network (ERC-20), with Stellar (SEP-41) and Circle's Arc (ERC-20) expected to connect in 2027.

entry.title: Visa and Mastercard adopt USDC payouts across 200 countries
entry.summary:
Visa and Mastercard are enabling USDC payouts across roughly 200 countries, extending stablecoin settlement through the two largest global card networks, according to CryptoSlate. The reported rollout would let payouts be routed in the dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle rather than solely through traditional correspondent banking rails.
Stablecoin settlement through Visa and Mastercard would move USDC from crypto-native venues into mainstream payment infrastructure used by merchants and financial institutions. Search context indicates card networks are already testing multiple stablecoins side by side for settlement, making this a live contest over which dollar tokens sit on those rails.
The report frames the move as a payout expansion spanning about 200 countries. Search excerpts note that Mastercard expanded its stablecoin settlement support in June 2026 to include USDC, PYUSD, RLUSD and SoFiUSD, and that SoFi became the first bank-issued stablecoin to go live on a major card network.

entry.title: BNY and Citadel Securities Use Tokenized Treasury in Overnight Repo
entry.summary:
BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) and market maker Citadel Securities executed an overnight repurchase agreement in which a tokenized Treasury was used, according to The Defiant. The transaction places a blockchain-represented government debt instrument inside a core short-term institutional funding trade rather than in a standalone tokenization pilot.
Overnight repo is the plumbing through which institutions borrow and lend cash against Treasuries, so using a tokenized Treasury there signals tokenized real-world assets edging from investment products into collateral and settlement functions.
The trade was structured as an overnight repo, a short-term secured loan in which securities are sold and repurchased the next day. It involved BNY, a major custodian bank, and Citadel Securities, one of the largest Treasury market intermediaries.

entry.title: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon among nine companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE
entry.summary:
Nine companies, including CoreWeave, Broadcom and Verizon, have objected to OKXICE facilitating tokenized trading of their shares, The Block reported on Oct 17, 2026. The objections raise legal and market-structure questions for tokenized equities.
According to the report, the objections raise legal and market-structure questions for tokenized equities, as listed issuers push back against third parties offering token versions of their shares.
OKXICE is the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) that filed with the SEC on Oct 5, 2026 to launch a tokenized securities platform. Its notice covered more than 60 companies currently listed on US stock exchanges.

entry.title: Strategy Slides 9.6% After MSCI Decision, Outpacing Bitcoin’s Drop
entry.summary:
Strategy's shares fell 9.6% following an MSCI decision, a drop larger than bitcoin's decline over the same period. The move outpaced the underlying asset that dominates the company's balance sheet.
The gap between the share move and bitcoin's decline points to the stock's sensitivity to index treatment, a factor separate from the price of the bitcoin it holds.
Strategy is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, and its equity is widely treated as a crypto-equity proxy. The decline exceeded bitcoin's own move rather than simply mirroring it.

entry.title: Binance Pool shuts on November 10, with record access ending two weeks later
entry.summary:
Binance Pool, the exchange's Bitcoin mining pool service, will shut down on November 10, and miners' access to their records will end two weeks after that date, giving users a deadline to move their operations elsewhere.
Miners who direct hashrate to Binance Pool must migrate to another pool before the November 10 shutdown, and the later record-access cutoff means payout and earnings data must be exported within that window.
Two separate deadlines apply: the pool itself stops operating on November 10, while access to records continues for two more weeks before ending.

entry.title: Google Quantum Chip Breakthrough: Cuts Error Rate in Key Computation, Quantum Risk to Early Bitcoin Wallets in Focus
entry.summary:
Google said its Willow quantum chip used a method called "Cultivation" to reduce errors in preparing magic states — a key resource for running quantum computations — by roughly 40 times, with the research published in Science this week. The experiment reached about 99.99% state fidelity, though only around 8% of attempts passed screening.
Google said the result could lower the hardware overhead of future large-scale quantum computers, and the advance has renewed attention on the long-term quantum risk to early Bitcoin wallets whose public keys are already exposed.
Researchers said the experiment still needs to be scaled up and that real-time operation and error correction remain to be solved. Google's earlier attack-cost estimates already assumed an efficient magic-state preparation scheme, so the 40x error reduction should not be read as a 40x cut in the cost of breaking Bitcoin.

entry.title: KOSPI erases an entire year’s worth of South Korean GDP
entry.summary:
South Korea's KOSPI index closed at 5,554 on Thursday, down 7.6% for the day after falling as much as 9.3% intraday, which triggered a 20-minute trading halt — its tenth circuit breaker of the year. The decline extended losses to seven consecutive sessions and left the index more than 40% below its June peak, wiping out over $2 trillion in market capitalization.
The more than $2 trillion decline exceeds South Korea's roughly $1.9 trillion annual economic output for 2025 and the approximately $1.6 trillion value of all bitcoin in existence. The rout has also downranked South Korea's market from sixth to 10th among the world's countries, from above $5 trillion in June.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together account for roughly half of KOSPI's market capitalization and have driven 70% of the drawdown since the June peak. Retail investors amplified the moves through leveraged single-stock ETFs, and the finance minister apologized for introducing those products; the Financial Services Commission chairman called an emergency meeting on Thursday, instructing financial firms to "maintain vigilance" and "actively respond to ensure financial market stability and investor protection."

entry.title: Charles Schwab Fully Opens Crypto Trading, CEO Says Crypto and Prediction Markets Will Expand Transaction Revenue
entry.summary:
Charles Schwab said on October 16 that it has completed the broad rollout of Schwab Crypto to eligible retail clients, who can now trade bitcoin and ether directly through Schwab.com, Schwab Mobile and thinkorswim. The company also began phased crypto deposit and withdrawal support and plans to add Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink by the end of 2026.
CEO Rick Wurster said at the company's fall business update that crypto trading will be an important channel for expanding transaction-based revenue, alongside new businesses such as prediction markets. The article states that with spot BTC and ETH trading live and SOL, AVAX and LINK to follow, competition between large traditional brokerages and crypto-native trading platforms will intensify further.
Trades are executed and sub-custodied by Paxos at a 0.75% fee, with individual transactions ranging from $1 to $2 million, and holdings appear alongside stocks, bonds and ETFs in existing Schwab accounts. Withdrawals require new addresses to be registered with a 24-hour waiting period and are capped at three per 24 hours and $5,000 each, monthly deposits can reach up to $50 million, and the service is not available to clients in New York, Louisiana, US territories or international clients; Schwab says its clients already hold about 20% of the industry's spot crypto ETF assets.

entry.title: Karpelès Reports Ledger Implants in Devices From Two More Resellers
entry.summary:
Karpelès reported discovering malicious implants in Ledger hardware wallet devices supplied by two additional resellers, extending reported supply-chain tampering beyond the reseller previously implicated.
If tampering extends beyond a single distribution channel, users who bought Ledger devices through third-party resellers rather than directly from the manufacturer face exposure, since an implant can capture recovery phrases during wallet setup.
Earlier reports tied the implants to devices distributed by CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller, with on-chain analysis estimating roughly $93 million drained from 311 wallets after seed phrases were captured during setup. Karpelès had previously flagged implant warnings months before the wider security crisis drew attention.

entry.title: MSCI’s new rules could squeeze Strategy’s Bitcoin buying machine
entry.summary:
CryptoSlate reports that MSCI’s revised index classification rules could reclassify Strategy (MSTR) — the largest corporate Bitcoin holder — as a fund or investment vehicle, which the report says could trigger an estimated $2.8 billion of forced selling by index funds tracking MSCI benchmarks. The impact is a prospective, rule-driven risk rather than a realized event.
Strategy funds much of its Bitcoin accumulation through equity issuance, so index-driven selling pressure on MSTR would hit the mechanism the company relies on to keep buying BTC. TD Cowen analysts cited in coverage argue that an MSCI exclusion would cause short-term disruption while longer-term adoption trends remain intact.
The roughly $2.8 billion figure is an estimate of forced index-fund selling and would only materialize if MSCI reclassifies the company. Strategy’s shares are included in benchmarks such as the Nasdaq 100 and MSCI indexes, which coverage notes have funneled crypto exposure into mainstream portfolios.

entry.title: Cobo Wallet announces service shutdown on December 1; users must transfer out assets in advance
entry.summary:
Cobo Wallet published an announcement on October 16 stating that its App service will officially shut down on December 1, 2026. Users must complete the transfer of all assets and update Cobo Wallet receiving addresses they previously set on other platforms before 23:59 on November 30.
Users who still store or receive assets through the Cobo Wallet App face a hard deadline, and the announcement says balances not moved before the shutdown will be treated as the user's acceptance of a monthly account management fee.
The management fee is calculated in coin terms at 2% of the remaining account assets per month, with a monthly minimum of the equivalent of US$100. The announcement did not explain the reason for the shutdown or disclose whether other Cobo products or its institutional business are affected.

entry.title: CME lists Uniswap futures on October 19: 10,000 UNI per standard contract
entry.summary:
CME will list Uniswap (UNI) futures on October 19, with each standard contract sized at 10,000 UNI. The listing gives regulated traders a new vehicle for exposure to the DeFi governance token.
A listing on CME, a major regulated derivatives venue, opens regulated futures exposure to UNI, a leading DeFi governance token, extending institutional access to the asset class.
The contract covers 10,000 UNI per standard contract and is scheduled to launch on October 19. The source describes it as a new vehicle for regulated exposure to the DeFi token.

entry.title: Marqeta and Coinbase partner to launch stablecoin payment card service
entry.summary:
Nasdaq-listed card-issuing platform Marqeta (MQ) and Coinbase have partnered to let crypto-native and non-crypto enterprises issue bank cards funded by stablecoin balances. Coinbase handles custody of the stablecoin balances and conversion between digital assets and fiat, Base provides on-chain settlement infrastructure, and Marqeta handles card issuance, payment processing and bank and card-network relationships.
Under the described division of labour, cardholders can spend stablecoin balances at merchants that accept bank cards worldwide, extending stablecoin use beyond crypto venues onto mainstream card rails. Enterprises can also issue cards and fund card programs around the clock.
Coinbase's role covers stablecoin balance custody and fiat conversion, while Base is named as the on-chain settlement layer. Marqeta had previously issued crypto asset payment cards for Coinbase.

entry.title: Reuters: Deutsche Bank to launch crypto custody in Germany within weeks, expand to Asia next year
entry.summary:
Deutsche Bank plans to launch a digital asset custody service in Germany within weeks, initially supporting BTC and ETH, with stablecoin on/off-ramp services to follow, its corporate bank co-head Gerald Podobnik told Reuters. The bank intends to extend the custody platform to Asian financial centres next year, and separately plans to offer tokenized deposits and help clients issue blockchain-based securities such as digital bonds.
A custody offering from Germany's largest bank would add a regulated venue in Europe for institutional BTC and ETH holdings, and the stated roadmap extends beyond custody into tokenized deposits and blockchain-based bond issuance. The launch is still tied to regulatory approval, which the bank has said it expects under MiCA.
The rollout is phased: custody of BTC, ETH and selected stablecoins including USDC, EURC and EURAU first, then fiat-to-stablecoin conversion. Podobnik said the move supports the bank's target of 8% compound annual growth in corporate banking by 2028; one report placed the Asia expansion in 2027 rather than "next year", and the bank's planned Asian target markets were not specified.

entry.title: Google demonstrates quantum computing breakthrough as observers weigh Q-day implications
entry.summary:
Google demonstrated a quantum computing breakthrough, prompting observers to assess what it means for Q-day — the point at which quantum machines could break the asymmetric encryption that secures blockchain networks and other systems. Coverage frames the advance as a capability milestone evaluated against future cryptographic implications rather than the arrival of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.
Observers weighing Q-day implications point to the public-key cryptography that secures most blockchains and digital systems in production today, which is why quantum progress by a leading lab draws scrutiny from the crypto industry even absent an immediate threat.
The development is described as a quantum computing advance demonstrated by Google, with implications assessed by observers rather than confirmed as a threat to deployed networks; it is not reported as a cryptographically relevant quantum computer capable of breaking RSA or elliptic-curve cryptography.

entry.title: Morning Minute: Solana Is About To Get Faster
entry.summary:
Solana has scheduled the mainnet activation of Alpenglow for October 21 at around 15:00 UTC, retiring the consensus mechanism it has run on since launch. Anza, the core development shop behind the upgrade, says finality will drop from roughly 12.8 seconds to a target of about 150 milliseconds — about 85 times faster.
Finality — the moment a transaction stops being reversible — has forced every exchange and payment processor to build around a roughly 13-second window, and the upgrade is intended to close it. The new mechanism is described as designed to survive 20% of stake acting maliciously plus another 20% simply offline, whereas the old system breaks if more than about a third of staked SOL turns hostile.
Because validators will vote directly to each other instead of casting votes as on-chain transactions, Solana's headline transaction count and TPS figures are expected to fall sharply even though users, volume and apps are unchanged. The upgrade is phase one of two, with no date yet for the second phase, and a previously announced September 28 activation date was announced and then pushed.

entry.title: Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express
entry.summary:
Ledger suspended its reseller network across South East Asia after thieves stole more than $103.4 million from 530 addresses using tampered Ledger devices inserted into the supply chain. Chainalysis reported that one of the affected holders was itself a task scammer who lost 60 Bitcoin (about $4.8 million) after buying three new Ledgers containing spyware that records seed phrases.
Ledger has asked resellers in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to remove its devices from sale, meaning buyers in those markets lose the local reseller channel while the tampering is investigated. Trezor also decided to shut some of its more far-flung resellers from Jan. 1, saying it cannot guarantee the same level of vigilance it applies closer to home.
Ledger insists that all confirmed thefts to date are from Asia, even though reports of tampered Ledgers in Europe prompted electronics retailer MediaMarkt to suspend sales. The roundup also notes that South Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit approved measures to block domestic access to 27 websites of unregistered exchanges and other virtual asset service providers including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex and Bitrue, and that Thailand's SEC finalized rules allowing Bitcoin and Ether ETFs to begin trading Friday.

entry.title: Schwab Completes Retail Bitcoin and Ether Rollout, Begins Crypto Transfers
entry.summary:
Charles Schwab has finished rolling out retail Bitcoin and Ether trading across its client base and has begun letting customers transfer crypto into and out of their Schwab accounts, according to The Defiant.
Adding transfers, not just buy-and-sell, changes what clients can do with digital assets once they are inside a large US retail brokerage account. The rollout extends spot crypto access to Schwab's retail client base.
The rollout covers Bitcoin and Ether for retail clients, with crypto transfers described as the newest part of the offering.

entry.title: Bitcoin Whipsaws as Crypto Liquidations Near $1 Billion
entry.summary:
Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Thursday for the first time in over a month, extending Wednesday's inflation-driven slide. CoinGlass data cited by Decrypt shows $948.22 million in crypto liquidations over 24 hours across 177,440 traders, with long positions accounting for $858.96 million, or 90.6%.
The move put U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF holders back underwater: Bitcoin is trading roughly 2% below that cohort's average cost basis near $82,300, a level it had closed above on 21 of the 24 days since September 21. Nexo analyst Iliya Kalchev called reclaiming that line "the first test of any rebound."
Ethereum led liquidations at $282.03 million, with Bitcoin just over $200 million, and the day ranked third-heaviest for long liquidations in 90 days behind October 8 and August 22. The largest single order was a $12.03 million Bitcoin long on Binance force-closed at $80,208.96; Bitcoin hit a low of $79,711 before buyers pulled it back near $80,925, with the RSI around 44.

entry.title: Mastercard and BVNK launch integrated fiat and stablecoin platform
entry.summary:
Mastercard and BVNK launched the Global Money Platform, a single-API product that lets banks, fintechs and enterprises embed multi-currency accounts holding fiat and stablecoins, with real-time conversion between them, stablecoin-linked cards and local bank payouts via Mastercard Move. The platform is already available through BVNK and is the first major integration of the two companies' capabilities since Mastercard completed its acquisition of BVNK in August.
It puts stablecoin balances directly inside Mastercard's card and payout rails rather than beside them, giving banks, fintechs and enterprises a single connection for holding, converting, sending and spending both forms of money. Nuvei and Marqeta, alongside Ontop, Beem and Almond FinTech, are among the first to integrate.
Mastercard said coverage for local-currency payouts through Mastercard Move is expected to reach more than 40 currencies across over 200 countries in 2027, with card issuing available in more than 130 countries. The company said the platform will add support for agentic commerce and tokenized deposits down the line.

entry.title: Stripe and Plasma to Develop Multi-Currency Stablecoin Cards
entry.summary:
Stripe announced it is partnering with Plasma to develop multi-currency stablecoin cards, with Plasma acting as a design partner on Stripe's stablecoin card-issuing infrastructure. The cards let individuals and businesses spend directly from balances they already hold — including USD, BRL, EUR, MXN, COP, USDC, OUSD and stablecoins compliant with the GENIUS Act — and are available in more than 30 countries today.
Stripe says the arrangement is intended to cut unnecessary currency conversions and foreign-exchange costs for cross-border payments, for example letting a user who holds euros spend directly in euros instead of converting to USD first.
Stripe also plans to let cardholders spend from multiple account balances with automatic selection of the appropriate currency at the point of purchase, and businesses will be able to issue cards matching their own spending currencies. The service is expected to expand from more than 30 countries today to over 100 countries in 2027; no transaction volumes or per-market launch dates were disclosed.

entry.title: ⚡️Ripple Prime launches RWA perpetual contracts for institutional clients, covering more than 100 markets
entry.summary:
Ripple's prime brokerage arm Ripple Prime is rolling out real-world asset (RWA) perpetual contracts to institutional clients, covering more than 100 reference markets including stocks, indices, ETFs and commodities, according to a Bloomberg report dated Oct. 15. The contracts are offered through Trade.xyz on Hyperliquid and support shared margin across positions, extending Ripple Prime's earlier opening of crypto perpetual trading to clients.
Ripple Prime International CEO Michael Higgins said the arrangement can help institutions improve capital efficiency and position management. Clients can pair the perpetual contracts with the underlying assets for basis trades or use them for directional exposure, including during traditional market closures and weekends.
Higgins also said traditional hedge funds are "very close" to directly participating in tokenized RWA markets, with the key being infrastructure that meets their counterparty and anti-money-laundering requirements. Over the past year, open interest in RWA perpetual contracts across major trading venues has grown from near zero to $9 billion, according to the report.

entry.title: Binance Pool is closing. Where will its Bitcoin miners go?
entry.summary:
Binance Pool is winding down its Bitcoin mining pool operation, with reports pointing to a shutdown on Nov. 10 after the pool's hashrate fell roughly 65%. Its miner base must now migrate hardware, payout settings and accounts to alternative pools.
The closure forces a redistribution of hash rate among the remaining Bitcoin mining pools, a shift that bears directly on mining concentration and on pool economics as displaced miners choose new operators.
The closure notice does not address the $500 million lending program Binance announced through the pool in October 2022, according to Mempool Brief. Alternative pools, including EMCD and OCEAN, are actively courting displaced Binance Pool miners.

entry.title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million to Expand Its Crypto Business
entry.summary:
Bloomberg reported that Binance.US is seeking to raise up to $100 million in a private funding round at a target valuation of roughly $1 billion, in order to expand its US operations. World Liberty Financial, a crypto venture linked to the Trump family, was made aware of the fundraising but is not participating.
The reported round would give the US affiliate fresh capital to expand at a time when it has lost significant market share following Binance's 2023 settlement with US authorities. The raise is being sought, not completed, and no terms have been disclosed.
Binance.US is exploring expansion into prediction markets, seeking to restore certain state money transmitter licenses, and considering external sources of trading liquidity that could potentially include Binance's global exchange, though no final decision has been made.

entry.title: SkyAI sells off large amounts of SOL; major shareholder Bastion Trading questions tender offer and demands full disclosure
entry.summary:
Nasdaq-listed Solana treasury company SkyAI has transferred out roughly 1.57 million SOL (~$175 million) since early October and has disclosed selling 1 million SOL (~$107 million), with a Form 8-K dated October 13 showing SOL holdings down to about 600,000 — roughly 70% below the "more than 2 million" figure it cited in mid-September. On October 14, 9.99% shareholder Bastion Trading said it will not participate in SkyAI's October 11 cash tender offer until its concerns are addressed, demanding full disclosure of the SOL disposals, an independent review, board changes, and a tender price of at least $3.50 per share instead of $3.00.
A listed Solana treasury company cutting its holdings by about 70% while crystallizing disclosed losses above $160 million, and a near-10% shareholder publicly contesting the buyout, put both the disclosure practices and board accountability of listed crypto-treasury vehicles in question.
On-chain data cited in the report indicates an average purchase price of about $194 per SOL, implying unrealized/realized losses above $160 million, and SkyAI has said it may continue selling. Bastion Trading also said that at the company's annual shareholder meeting, all five incumbent directors received far more abstentions than votes in favor, some approaching three to one, and questioned whether the board still has a shareholder mandate to sell core reserves and pursue the tender offer.

entry.title: Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme
entry.summary:
Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme, and its Open Money Stack is now a US-regulated payments platform that supports USD inflows via bank transfer, card, or cash deposits for on-chain settlement. Named clients include Tazapay, Mesh, Toku, and Kira.
The deal folds regulated US money-transmission capability into Polygon's payments stack, giving the Open Money Stack a fiat on-ramp channel through which bank, card, or cash dollars can be moved on-chain for settlement.
BlockBeats reported that the platform covers 48 US states, holds 37 state-level money transmitter licenses plus 11 applicable exemptions, and is registered with FinCEN as a money services business; the first customers use it for cross-border business payments, account top-ups, global payroll, and USD services.

entry.title: Evernorth Partners With Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo to Deploy $648 Million XRP Reserve
entry.summary:
Nasdaq-listed Evernorth has selected Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo as its first institutional partners to deploy roughly 473 million XRP, worth about $648 million at current prices, through institutional strategies starting in the fourth quarter. The company said it will later expand into lending on the XRP Ledger and on-chain DeFi strategies, with the deployment led by former Coinbase Asset Management co-CIO Hugo Jeandesboz.
A publicly listed treasury company is naming regulated exchanges and custodians to actively put a nine-figure XRP reserve to work rather than simply holding it, which ties a large XRP position into established institutional custody and trading venues.
The plan is a stated intention to deploy from the fourth quarter onward, not a completed deployment. The 473 million XRP figure is valued at approximately $648 million at current prices, and the XRP Ledger lending and on-chain DeFi expansion is described as a future step.

entry.title: Crypto exchange Kraken owner to buy European bank
entry.summary:
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank for an undisclosed amount, a deal that would give it a European Union banking license. The acquisition is subject to regulatory approval and is expected to close in 2027.
The deal would let Payward offer EU customers interest-bearing deposits, loans, card services and euro payments, expanding it beyond crypto trading, and would make it the first crypto firm to buy a European bank, according to the Financial Times.
Saldo Bank had €163.9 million (about $180 million) in total assets at the end of 2025, up 22.7% year over year, and is licensed in Lithuania, Finland, Sweden and Germany with a passport to operate in the Netherlands; it offers deposits, consumer and business loans and payment services. Payward said its banking business has already originated more than $2 billion in loans and holds a Federal Reserve limited-purpose master account and an electronic money institution license in Ireland.

entry.title: Ledger asks distributors in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to stop selling hardware wallets amid tampering investigation
entry.summary:
Ledger asked resellers and distributors in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to suspend sales and take its hardware wallets off the shelves while it investigates suspected device tampering, the company said in a post on X on Tuesday. The request expands earlier stop-sale and shipment-suspension measures against regional reseller CryptoBilis, an investigation made public on Oct 9.
The move removes Ledger devices from retail shelves across a region and puts the integrity of the hardware-wallet supply chain, a core assumption of self-custody, under scrutiny. In Germany, MediaMarkt Saturn stopped selling Ledger devices in stores and online with Ledger's agreement after a customer reported an implant, though no funds were lost.
Ledger's Donjon security team found the implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the device's screen during setup and sends it out over LTE; anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and move its funds. Onchain investigator Specter has traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.

entry.title: Strategy’s USD Cash down 60% in seven weeks
entry.summary:
Strategy’s USD Cash fell 60% from $1.61 billion on August 30 to $640.5 million on October 11, according to the company’s latest disclosure this week. Most of the spending went to buybacks of STRC, its high-yield dividend preferred stock, which had briefly collapsed to $71.25 from a $90–100.03 offering range.
The buybacks consumed cash that Strategy had mostly raised by diluting MSTR common shareholders, and at the disclosed pace its USD Cash would run out in roughly four weeks if not topped up. The company is the largest corporate bitcoin treasury holder, so its dollar liquidity bears on how much room it has to keep accumulating BTC.
Strategy’s August USD Cash figure included expected, not-yet-settled stock sale proceeds, which the company footnoted. A separate “USD Reserve,” earmarked for bond coupons and dividends, stood at $4.88 billion on October 11, down from $5.10 billion on August 30 — a combined decline of about 18%. Strategy’s board doubled the STRC buyback authorization to $2 billion in September, with just $354.8 million of that remaining as of October 11.

entry.title: Bitcoin falls below $82,000 as hotter core CPI revives Fed hike concerns
entry.summary:
Bitcoin dropped below $82,000 after a hotter-than-expected core CPI reading renewed expectations that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates, The Block reported on Oct. 14. The decline followed the release of the inflation data, which pointed to firmer underlying price pressures.
Rate expectations are a primary channel through which macro data hits risk-asset pricing, and the move shows bitcoin trading in line with that sensitivity. Bloomberg data cited by Livemint showed that in 8 of the last 10 Fed hikes, bitcoin was lower a month later.
Core CPI tracks consumer price changes while excluding food and energy, which tend to be more volatile. The report was published on Oct. 14.

entry.title: 'It Can Take Years': Coinbase Presses for Bitcoin Quantum Migration to Start Now
entry.summary:
Coinbase published a blog post on Tuesday urging Bitcoin developers to begin quantum-resistance preparations immediately, warning that consensus changes and ecosystem migrations "can take years." The exchange, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin, laid out technical requirements including support for a flexible "container" design such as BIP-360, a staged "1-of-2" classical-plus-quantum spending path, compatibility with the MPC key-splitting used by custodians, and separate governance for dormant and Satoshi-era coins.
The post is positioned as a set of requirements from one of the network's largest stakeholders rather than a mandate, and it is a proposal rather than a deployed upgrade or consensus change. Coinbase argues that waiting for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer to be announced would leave too little time to respond.
Coinbase stressed that any transition would need to protect both existing and newly created coins, fit Bitcoin's limited block space, work for ordinary wallets and institutional custody alike, and offer a migration path for coins that never move. It said dormant, lost, or exposed coins including Satoshi-era holdings are a separate governance problem, and cautioned that any rescue mechanism must itself be quantum-safe so that an attacker with only an exposed public key could not exploit it.

entry.title: DriveWealth to use Ripple's RLUSD for stablecoin settlement, cross-border payments
entry.summary:
DriveWealth, a brokerage-as-a-service platform, announced a partnership with Ripple to integrate blockchain capabilities — stablecoin settlement, payments, custody and prime brokerage — into its global investment infrastructure. The collaboration focuses first on integrating Ripple's stablecoin infrastructure in Europe, with plans to extend to the United States and other markets.
DriveWealth supplies API-based trading infrastructure to banks, fintechs, broker-dealers and consumer brands, so the tie-up would push an existing enterprise stablecoin into brokerage settlement and cross-border funding rails if implemented. The arrangement was announced as a plan rather than a completed integration.
The stated scope includes access to Ripple Payments to streamline cross-border fund inflows, digital asset custody in Europe with later expansion to other markets, and exploration of institutional business such as equities financing through Ripple Prime. No timeline, transaction volumes or commercial terms were disclosed.

entry.title: Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets
entry.summary:
Trezor has told partners in its authorized reseller network that their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, and that it will ship them no new stock, days after rival Ledger's Donjon security team confirmed a hidden spy implant in hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Trezor said there is "not a single piece of evidence" its own devices were compromised and described the cut as a precaution.
The Ledger finding is a confirmed supply-chain compromise of seed-phrase handling in widely used hardware wallets, and Trezor's decision shows the incident is already reshaping how wallet makers manage third-party distribution.
Ledger says the CryptoBilis implant reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears, then sends it out over LTE via an eSIM, without altering the key-storage chip or the operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally. Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified; Trezor has not said how many resellers are affected, and those cut can keep selling existing stock through the holiday season.

entry.title: Solana consensus upgrade Alpenglow to go live on mainnet on October 21, cutting finality to about 150 milliseconds
entry.summary:
Anza, Solana's core development team, announced that the Alpenglow consensus upgrade is scheduled to activate on Solana mainnet-beta around October 21 at 22:50 (UTC+8, roughly 14:50 UTC), with the migration to be completed within a single slot. Alpenglow replaces TowerBFT, the consensus protocol Solana has used since genesis, and is intended to cut transaction finality from seconds to about 150 milliseconds.
Anza says moving voting off-chain frees block space for user transactions, and that faster finality shortens settlement for institutions from the usual 1–3 business days to roughly 150 milliseconds. It is described as the most significant change to Solana's core consensus since the network launched.
Anza developed Alpenglow over 18 months; it was previously migrated on testnet (September 24) and devnet (September 25) and tested in a 1,500-node simulation, with a bug bounty exceeding 25,000 SOL. Under the new Votor voting protocol, validators exchange votes directly instead of submitting them as on-chain transactions, which the announcement says could cause a significant decline in reported transaction totals that include validator votes.

entry.title: XRPN took shareholder vote with no knowledge of XRP inflation bug
entry.summary:
A newly disclosed bug in the XRP Ledger's base-layer payment engine could have allowed an attacker to mint trillions of new XRP for almost nothing; researcher Cayden Liao and Veria AI reported it on September 22, and Ripple shipped a closed-source fix in xrpld 3.4.1 on September 25 described only as "integer-arithmetic hardening." Shareholders of the Ripple/Arrington-backed XRP treasury vehicle Evernorth (XRPN) voted on their plan without being told about the flaw, and an official report admitting what the patch actually fixed appeared only on October 9, the day the merger closed.
The flaw meant XRP's fixed supply of 100 billion — the core claim underpinning Evernorth's treasury plan — was technically unenforceable on the network for roughly a decade. The episode also raises governance questions, since XRPN shareholders made redemption and merger decisions inside a window in which Ripple knew about the bug but they did not.
According to the report, the bug likely dated back to 2015 and a single validated transaction using the exploit "could have created spendable XRP far beyond the total supply." The patch shipped without an amendment vote, and no actual exploitation of the vulnerability has been reported.

entry.title: BNY, Citadel Securities test tokenized U.S. Treasuries to speed up Wall Street financing
entry.summary:
BNY, described as the world's largest custody bank, and trading firm Citadel Securities said on Tuesday they had completed a transaction using tokenized U.S. Treasuries, showing how blockchain-based government bonds could move from settlement into financing. BNY also said it plans to add digital cash and tokenized deposit capabilities and to extend the operating hours of its traditional settlement systems for Federal Reserve-eligible securities and U.S. triparty transactions, with the aim of reaching European and Asian trading hours next year.
The effort targets a key bottleneck in financial markets: moving government bonds used as collateral for trading and borrowing can take time, tying up assets that could otherwise be put to work. Citadel Securities digital assets operations lead Dan Doherty said efficient movement of high-quality collateral is fundamental to well-functioning markets and that reducing delays across the trade lifecycle could improve how institutional markets operate.
The transaction was a demonstration of how tokenized government bonds could move from settlement into financing, potentially letting firms reuse collateral sooner and free up cash for other trades. BNY chief innovation and market transformation officer Carolyn Weinberg said using a tokenized representation of a U.S. Treasury across both settlement and financing enables a more connected, efficient and always-on financial system.

entry.title: Ethereum Name Service plans major .eth overhaul with one irreversible catch for domain holders
entry.summary:
Ethereum Name Service is planning a major overhaul of .eth domains that, according to CryptoSlate, includes an irreversible catch for domain holders. Coverage of the proposal points to an ENSv2 upgrade featuring a one-way domain migration option.
The change targets .eth, ENS's core naming product, and the described one-way migration gives holders a decision that reportedly cannot be reversed once taken. ENS's own FAQ states that existing name ownership would be preserved through the ENSv2 transition.
Coverage of the proposal cites an irreversible, one-way domain migration, support for stablecoin payments, and a 60% fee increase for five-character names. ENS's ENSv2 page describes a protocol rebuilt from the ground up with a new ownership model and new apps.

entry.title: Interactive Brokers Launches Ethereum Staking Through Zerohash
entry.summary:
Interactive Brokers (NASDAQ: IBKR) has launched cryptocurrency staking, with infrastructure provided by digital asset firm zerohash. Initially, eligible Interactive Brokers LLC clients can stake ETH through the Staking Dashboard in IBKR's Client Portal, where they submit staking and unstaking requests and monitor pending activity.
IBKR CEO Milan Galik said the staking service lets clients earn additional yield on the crypto assets they hold, similar to the firm's stock yield enhancement program. It extends ETH staking access to a mainstream brokerage customer base.
Rewards, when earned, are credited as additional staked cryptocurrency and can compound while the position remains staked. IBKR currently supports trading in 20 digital assets and accepts deposits in USDC, RLUSD and PYUSD.
